description: fnet v1.0.0's fhttp HTTP/1.1 server: fnet's epoll event loops find where each request message ends and enqueue it, then the standard library parses it and runs an http.Handler on a task-pool worker, so there is no goroutine per connection. Responses are buffered whole. A request whose body is not buffered (larger than 1MB, chunked, or framed unusually) is handed to an internal net/http server, which closes that connection after the one request. fnet's ReusePort option is on: on Linux every sub-reactor listens on :8080 with a socket of its own, sharing the port through SO_REUSEPORT so the kernel spreads the connections over the loops. A second fhttp.Server on :8081 speaks HTTPS through fnet's ftls (crypto/tls inside the connection callbacks, ALPN http/1.1) for the TLS profiles. Static files are read per request from the mounted directory, serving the pre-compressed .br/.gz siblings when the client accepts them; /async-db and the crud routes use pgx's pool sized from DATABASE_MAX_CONN, with Redis as a cache-aside store for item reads where REDIS_URL is provided.
